solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Lurid tabloid upset by his exploitation

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so the word ends up the other way round
exploitation means working something over for your own ends, so these letters get reworked

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a low-grade newspaper
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid is thrown into turmoil after being exploited by some man.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG turned over gives GAR, and HIS rearranged gives ISH: GAR + ISH = GARISH. 'Lurid tabloid' reads as one phrase, but the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe colours or styles that are showy, glaring and in poor taste.

clue.text: Grotesque type of boiled 'egg Royal'

indicators.note: boiling churns and scrambles what is in the pan, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky swipe at some royal figure portrayed as a boiled egg, a regular Private Eye style of mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''egg' mimics a Cockney accent, which helps disguise EGG ROYAL as the fodder for GARGOYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gargoyle is a carved grotesque on a church roof, and the word is also used of an ugly-looking person.

clue.text: Try to get elected and, having got elected, quarrel!

blocks.note: to run for office is to stand as a candidate
a winning candidate is said to be in

explanation.surface: The familiar arc of a politician: campaign, win, then immediately start fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'elected' is deliberate: the first is part of the phrase for standing, the second on its own means IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal noun for an argument or clash with somebody, often with authority.

clue.text: Political slant – dodgy (which is a benefit, incidentally)

blocks.note: spin is the slanted presentation of news by politicians
food that is dodgy has gone off

explanation.surface: A cynical aside that political spin is shady, though it does bring some benefit on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a throwaway aside, but it holds the definition; 'incidentally' is part of it, not a comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-off is a secondary, unplanned advantage or product arising from some other main activity.

clue.text: Shit! Cyclops encounters disheartened Tory coarseness

indicators.note: losing heart means losing the central part, leaving only the outside letters

blocks.note: crud is slang for filth or muck
the setter refers to themself, so I
only the first and last letters survive

explanation.surface: The setter swears on meeting a dispirited Conservative and deplores their vulgarity.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so it stands for I. Crossword setters often refer to themselves by name to mean I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Crudity and coarseness are synonyms for rough, vulgar or unrefined behaviour or language.

clue.text: Fruity thing got out of bed with joint

blocks.note: past tense of rise, to get up
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A randy person gets up from bed with a spliff in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests something saucy, and 'joint' something smoked; both are innocent here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose hip is the red fleshy fruit of the rose plant, used for syrup and tea.

clue.text: One who's tried to stand by worker

blocks.note: to stand by someone is to support or defend them
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Someone who has made an effort to support a colleague on the shop floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried to' reads as 'attempted to', but 'tried' belongs to the definition in its courtroom sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant is the person accused in court whose case is heard before a judge or jury.

clue.text: Temperature over the country's doubled rather basic transport

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
the country is the United Kingdom
the pair so far is written out a second time

explanation.surface: A complaint that Britain's temperature has doubled, and its transport is fairly primitive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' puts T above UK; the pair is then written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuk tuk is a three-wheeled motorised rickshaw used as a cheap taxi across South and South-East Asia.

clue.text: Chlorine dumped on island by China – catastrophe our politicians only pay lip service to

definitions.text: our politicians only pay lip service to
definitions.note: a clause describing the answer: the thing our politicians only pay lip service to

blocks.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
I is a common abbreviation for island
Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate
a catastrophe is a crisis

explanation.surface: Chemical pollution dumped on an island by China is an environmental disaster that politicians only talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: In rhyming slang 'china' (china plate) means mate, a friend. The capital C disguises it as the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians are routinely accused of voicing concern about global warming emergencies without taking real action.

clue.text: Maybe our Brian's nursing broken lip – them's the rules!

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so the letters are rearranged
to nurse is to cradle in your arms, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Private Eye calls Prince Charles 'Brian', so this is a prince's, PRINCE'S
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Private Eye's Brian is tending an injured lip, and someone says that's just how things are.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye nicknames the royal family: the Queen was Brenda and Charles is Brian. 'Maybe' marks Brian as just one example of a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles are fundamental rules or moral codes that govern conduct, which is what the colloquial phrase announces.

clue.text: (& 24ac.) Put on the latest typical Trumpian retort?

blocks.note: to put on an accent or feeling is to feign or counterfeit it
the latest is the most recent information or report of events

explanation.surface: Dressing up in the newest fashion, or the standard Trump response to anything he dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on the latest' reads as wearing new clothes; split it into two synonyms instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump habitually dismissed critical reporting as a hoax with this dismissive phrase.

clue.text: see 23ac.
After ball, getting madly horny? No, um – truly

indicators.note: acting madly means acting wildly and without order, so these letters get scrambled
coming after something means being placed behind it in the answer

blocks.note: a ball is round, like the letter O
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A reveller swears they didn't get randy after the dance; 'ball' is a party, not the letter shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball here is the round shape giving O, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is on your honour pledges that it is sincerely true, like saying truly or honestly.

clue.text: Rather constrained Conservative needs to drop temper tantrum

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a noun: something that is a close fit is rather constrained

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to drop something is to lose it
a fit of temper

explanation.surface: An uptight Tory is advised to stop throwing tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather constrained' reads like a description of the Tory but it is the definition, loosely matching a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A close fit is a tight squeeze, leaving little room to move, so it is snug and restricting.

clue.text: Ed's 'carbon-free' cash cow brazenly put on display

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so that letter is removed
brazen behaviour ignores the proper order, so these letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
C is the chemical symbol for carbon, the letter to be removed
taken as written, then reduced and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband's green policy is paraded as a shameless money-spinner; Ed Miliband is the UK energy secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one C from CASHCOW to leave ASHCOW, then rearrange it with EDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To showcase something is to exhibit it prominently so that others can see and admire it.

clue.text: Pence: firstly "traitor", then "knucklehead"

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Mike Pence was called a traitor by Trump supporters and then an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a list of insults; the first becomes a piece and the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a foolish or stupid person, much like a knucklehead.

clue.text: OK, maybe Tom wants drink

blocks.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so Tom is an example of a Thumb
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that Tom is probably after a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' shows Tom is only one Thumb, the one in the fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up is a gesture or sign of approval, the same as giving something the OK.

clue.text: Love second hospital situated under Conservative Club!

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
love is zero in tennis, O
S is the abbreviation for second
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone adores a second hospital built beneath a Tory members' club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative Club' looks like one name, but it splits: C comes first and 'Club' is the definition. A cosh is a short heavy stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a British word for a short heavy truncheon used as a weapon, which is a kind of club.

clue.text: Progress made with oral sex method

blocks.note: head is slang for oral sex
a method is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A sex manual claims a certain technique produces progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Typical Private Eye smut: the crude slang gives the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: To make headway is to advance or move forward, so the noun means progress towards a goal.

clue.text: Fast movers, spoken of as unfaithful types

indicators.note: something spoken of is said out loud, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: unfaithful partners are cheaters

explanation.surface: Serial philanderers who move quickly from one partner to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, capable of short sprints of around seventy miles an hour.

clue.text: Text re. Melania's houses over the top

indicators.note: a house holds things inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: running across the words

explanation.surface: A message about Melania Trump's many homes that is way over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from inside 'Text' across 're.' into 'Melania's'. 'Houses' looks like her properties but is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the top is an idiom for excessive or exaggerated, meaning far beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Request by climber to get into lap dancing

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it
dancing letters move around and change places

blocks.note: apes are climbing animals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer asks to be allowed into a lap-dancing club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lap dancing' reads as a strip-club term; here 'lap' is fodder and 'dancing' scrambles it once APE is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An appeal is an earnest plea or formal request for help, money or reconsideration.

clue.text: Sporty Spice, top tier consultant?

indicators.note: sporty suggests jumping around energetically, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Sporty Spice, of the Spice Girls, is apparently now an elite advisor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporty Spice' is a Spice Girl's nickname, but 'Sporty' is the anagram signal. The question mark shows a consultant is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a consultant is a senior doctor who is an expert in one field of medicine.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) At a loss for words? Not working? Keep it pretty basic

blocks.note: unable to speak
a system that is not working is said to be out of action, the opposite of up

explanation.surface: A series of questions about someone speechless and idle, followed by advice to keep things simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The two questions are separate pieces; the final instruction is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumb down is to simplify material so that it is less demanding or intellectually challenging.

clue.text: Non-PC attractive woman welcomes head from rogue – laughable

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: doll is a dated, sexist word for an attractive woman, hence non-PC
the first letter

explanation.surface: An attractive woman takes in the leader of some scoundrels, and it's absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-PC' tells you the word for the woman is dated and sexist.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry or whimsical way, so something droll is funny and causes laughter.

clue.text: see 10ac.
How The i moved to exploit Biden & co

indicators.note: things that are moved change position, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to exploit is to use

explanation.surface: A question about how the i newspaper shifted its stance to take advantage of the Biden administration.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national newspaper, which makes 'The i' look like a title rather than fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The White House is used by metonymy for the US president and his administration, here Biden and his staff.

clue.text: Happy with our mag's sexy look?

blocks.note: glad means happy
the setter's magazine is Private Eye, often just called the Eye

explanation.surface: Is Private Eye satisfied with its seductive new design?
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in Private Eye, so 'our mag' is the Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the glad eye is an old-fashioned British idiom for a flirtatious or inviting glance.

clue.text: Get tearful from my having an erection

blocks.note: both are exclamations of surprise
crude slang: aroused

explanation.surface: Someone is moved to tears by their own arousal, in true Private Eye fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation, as in 'My, my!'
explanation.definitionFit: When tears well up they rise in the eyes, so a person welling up is starting to cry.
